# Business Requirements Document — Automated Customer Data Ingestion Pipeline

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Generated by:** brd-story-creator skill
**Source:** MEETING TRANSCRIPT — CUSTOMER DATA.txt (from @DE_POC.PUBLIC.BRD_REQUIREMENTS_STAGE)

---

## 1. Business Context

The organization currently ingests customer data from an external source system into Snowflake through a manual process. As data volumes and frequency of updates grow, this manual approach is unsustainable, error-prone, and lacks traceability. There is a business need to automate this ingestion to support downstream analytics with reliable, timely, and validated customer data.

## 2. Problem Statement

- No automation — data loads require manual intervention each time.
- No incremental processing — the full dataset is reloaded, wasting compute and risking duplication.
- No validation — invalid or malformed records may be silently loaded into the target.
- No traceability — there is no load tracking (batch ID, source file, row counts, processing status).
- No error handling — failed records are not captured, logged, or available for investigation/reprocessing.

## 3. Current State (AS-IS)

- Customer data is manually extracted from the source system and loaded into Snowflake.
- Full reloads are performed each time, with no incremental or CDC-based processing.
- No validation is applied to incoming data before loading.
- No duplicate detection or prevention mechanism exists.
- No error logging or failed-record capture is in place.
- No batch/load tracking metadata is recorded.

## 4. Desired State (TO-BE)

- Automated pipeline ingests customer data without manual intervention.
- Incremental/CDC-based processing for new and changed records only.
- Data validated before loading; invalid records rejected and logged.
- Duplicate records detected and prevented.
- Load tracking with metadata: load ID, source file, timestamp, row count, status.
- Error log captures failed records for investigation and reprocessing.
- Processed data available in Snowflake for downstream analytics.
- Pipeline is repeatable and idempotent.

## 5. Stakeholders

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|---------------|
| Product Owner | Defines business requirements, approves pipeline behavior |
| Business Analyst | Documents requirements, validates business rules |
| Data Engineer | Designs and implements the automated pipeline |
| QA Engineer | Validates record counts, duplicate handling, incremental logic, error handling |
| Downstream Analytics Users | Consume the processed customer data |

## 6. Scope

### In-Scope
- Automated ingestion from source to Snowflake
- Incremental/CDC processing
- Data validation and invalid record rejection
- Duplicate detection and prevention
- Load tracking metadata
- Error logging
- Downstream analytics availability

### Out-of-Scope
- Source system modifications
- Downstream dashboards or reports
- Non-customer data entities
- Real-time/streaming ingestion
- Data masking or PII handling

## 7. Success Criteria

- Pipeline runs end-to-end without manual intervention.
- Only new/changed records processed (incremental/CDC).
- Zero duplicates in target after execution.
- Invalid records rejected and logged.
- Load tracking for each batch.
- Data queryable for downstream analytics.
- Idempotent — no duplicates or reloads on rerun.

## 8. Constraints & Assumptions

### Constraints
- All processing within Snowflake.
- Use existing COMPUTE_WH warehouse.
- Adhere to existing role and access policies.

### Assumptions
- Source data available in a Snowflake stage.
- Source data contains unique customer identifier.
- File format/data contract defined during implementation.

## 9. Dependencies

- Source system provides data in agreed format to accessible stage.
- DE_POC.PUBLIC database/schema exist.
- File format available.
- COMPUTE_WH warehouse available.

## 10. Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Source format changes | Pipeline failures | Data contract + schema validation |
| Large volumes | Performance issues | Incremental processing + warehouse tuning |
| Dedup misses edge cases | Duplicates in target | QA testing with edge cases |
| Error log unmonitored | Failed records accumulate | Monitor + alert on threshold |
| Source data delayed | Stale analytics data | Load status tracking + alerts |
